question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

(They have been) dejected when he arrived, but now they sparkle with enthusiasm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. They had been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contrasts an earlier past state with the present ("but now they sparkle with enthusiasm"). The earlier state must therefore be in the past perfect tense — had + V3.

◦ Correct: They had been dejected when he arrived, but now they sparkle with enthusiasm.

• "Dejected" (उदास / निराश) here works as an adjective, so it needs a form of the verb "be": had been dejected.

• The clause "when he arrived" fixes a point in the past; the state of being dejected existed up to and around that point, which is exactly what the past perfect expresses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "They were been" is grammatically impossible — "were" and "been" cannot stand together without "have/had".

• Option 3 "They was" has a subject-verb agreement error: the plural subject "They" takes "were", never "was".

• Option 4 "No correction required" is wrong because "They have been dejected ... but now they sparkle" mixes a present-perfect state with a contrasting present, which is illogical here.

NOTE

• Tense rule for SSC: Past Perfect = had + past participle (V3) is used for the earlier of two past situations, or for a past state that ended before a later past/present reference point.

• Sequence to remember: had been (earlier past) → was/were (past) → have/has been (up to now) → am/is/are (now).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Ancient Indians were never this ______ minded.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. narrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed compound adjective is "narrow-minded", meaning not willing to accept ideas or opinions different from one's own; intolerant / prejudiced. (संकीर्ण सोच वाला)

◦ Correct: Ancient Indians were never this narrow minded.

• The sentence praises the openness of ancient Indians, so the word that fits the blank must describe mental rigidity — and English has only one standard collocation for that: narrow + minded.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cramp minded" — "cramp" means a sudden painful tightening of a muscle; there is no such compound.

• Option 2 "slim minded" — "slim" refers to a thin body or a slight chance ("a slim chance"), never to the mind.

• Option 4 "tiny minded" — "tiny" means very small in size; the accepted expression is "narrow-minded" (or the rarer "small-minded"), not "tiny-minded".

NOTE

• Common "-minded" compounds asked in SSC: narrow-minded (intolerant), broad-minded / open-minded (liberal), absent-minded (forgetful), strong-minded (determined), like-minded (sharing the same views), single-minded (fully focused).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Susan had recently run on to / Catherine at the supermarket, they / were seeing each other after many years.
option_1: were seeing each other after many years.
option_4: Susan had recently run on to
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Susan had recently run on to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb that means to meet somebody by chance is "run into", not "run on to".

◦ Correct: Susan had recently run into Catherine at the supermarket, they were seeing each other after many years.

• "Run on to" is not a standard phrasal verb in this sense; the error therefore lies in the first segment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment 2 ("Catherine at the supermarket, they") is fine — it simply carries the object and the pronoun of the next clause.

• Segment 3 ("were seeing each other after many years.") is acceptable: the past continuous is used here for the meeting that was taking place.

NOTE

• High-frequency phrasal verbs with "run" for SSC:

◦ run into = to meet unexpectedly / to collide with (अचानक मिलना)

◦ run out of = to exhaust the supply of something

◦ run over = to knock down and pass over with a vehicle

◦ run down = to criticise, or to lose power

◦ run after = to chase / to pursue

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A person who likes humankind and human society
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Philanthropist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "philanthropist" is a person who loves humankind and works for the welfare of society, usually by donating money, time or effort to good causes. (परोपकारी / मानव-प्रेमी)

◦ Root: Greek philos = loving + anthropos = human being.

• The definition given — "a person who likes humankind and human society" — is the textbook one-word substitution for philanthropist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Lunatic = a person who is mentally ill or behaves in an extremely foolish way. (पागल)

• Option 2 Narcissist = a person who is excessively in love with himself/herself and his/her own appearance. (आत्ममुग्ध)

• Option 3 Mercenary = a soldier who fights for any country or group that pays him; as an adjective, motivated only by money. (भाड़े का सैनिक)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions frequently asked:

◦ Misanthrope = one who hates humankind (the antonym of philanthropist)

◦ Philanthropy = the practice of helping humankind

◦ Altruist = one who works selflessly for others

◦ Egotist = one who talks constantly about himself

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

He hesitated, studying her face with a (confused) expression.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. puzzled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Confused" means unable to understand something clearly; bewildered. (भ्रमित / उलझन में)

• "Puzzled" carries exactly the same sense — unable to understand; perplexed. (चकित / असमंजस में)

◦ Correct: He hesitated, studying her face with a puzzled expression.

• Both words describe the same facial state — one of not understanding what is going on — so they are true synonyms in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 calm = peaceful, free from excitement — the opposite of the disturbed state implied by "confused".

• Option 2 assisted = helped or supported; it has nothing to do with mental confusion.

• Option 3 explicated = explained something in detail; an "explicated expression" is not idiomatic English.

NOTE

• Synonyms of confused: puzzled, perplexed, bewildered, baffled, disoriented, muddled, nonplussed.

• Antonyms of confused: clear, certain, enlightened, aware, lucid.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Go bananas
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To become excited or angry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "go bananas" means to become extremely excited, wildly enthusiastic, or very angry — to behave in a crazy way. (आपे से बाहर हो जाना / बहुत उत्तेजित हो जाना)

◦ Example: The crowd went bananas when the last-ball six was hit.

◦ Example: My father went bananas when he saw the broken window.

• The idiom therefore covers both extremes of losing self-control — wild excitement and rage — which is precisely what Option 1 states.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To win a match" — no idiom "go bananas" carries any sense of winning.

• Option 3 "To finish household chores" — unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

• Option 4 "To feel low" — this is the opposite; "go bananas" implies high, uncontrolled emotion, not sadness.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of losing control: go nuts, go crazy, go berserk, hit the roof, fly off the handle, blow one's top, lose one's cool.

• Other fruit/food idioms: the apple of one's eye (very dear one), a piece of cake (very easy), spill the beans (reveal a secret), top banana (the most important person).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Evidence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Concealment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evidence" means facts, signs or proof that are made available or brought to light to prove something. (साक्ष्य / प्रमाण)

• "Concealment" means the act of hiding something or keeping it secret. (छिपाना / गोपन)

◦ Evidence brings facts out into the open; concealment keeps them hidden — hence they are direct opposites.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Signature = a person's name written by himself; not an opposite of evidence.

• Option 3 Information = facts or knowledge about something; this is closer to a synonym of evidence, not an antonym.

• Option 4 Duplicity = deceitfulness, double-dealing; it means dishonesty in behaviour, not the hiding of proof, so it is not the best antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of evidence: proof, testimony, corroboration, substantiation, documentation.

• Antonyms of evidence: concealment, suppression, disproof, refutation.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the (bracketed) word in the given sentence.

Given (sufficient) effort, all known infectious agents can be specifically identified.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. optimal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sufficient" means just as much as is needed; barely adequate. (पर्याप्त)

• "Optimal" means the best or most favourable possible; the maximum that can be achieved. (इष्टतम / सर्वोत्तम)

◦ On the scale of quantity/quality, "sufficient" sits at the bare minimum required, while "optimal" sits at the best possible level — so among the four choices given, "optimal" is the word that stands at the opposite end from "sufficient".

◦ Substituted: Given optimal effort, all known infectious agents can be specifically identified.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 unrefined = not purified, crude or unpolished; it is the opposite of "refined", not of "sufficient".

• Option 3 trivial = of little value or importance; it is the opposite of "important/significant", not of "sufficient".

• Option 4 captivity = the state of being imprisoned; it is a noun and cannot replace the adjective "sufficient" at all.

• Note also that only Options 1, 2 and 3 are adjectives, and of these only optimal contrasts with "sufficient" in the required sense of degree.

NOTE

• Vocabulary set: sufficient / adequate / enough (just what is needed) ↔ optimal / maximal / ideal (the very best) ↔ insufficient / deficient / scanty (less than needed).

• Related word: optimum (noun/adjective) = the most favourable condition; optimise = to make as effective as possible.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

And to think after all these years you still have the ______ to say such things to me!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. arrogance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arrogance" means an offensive display of superiority; overbearing pride and insolence. (घमंड / अहंकार)

◦ Correct: And to think after all these years you still have the arrogance to say such things to me!

• The exclamatory tone with "And to think ... you still have the ______ to say such things" expresses indignation — the speaker is accusing the listener of insolent boldness. The noun that captures this is arrogance (compare the common expressions "to have the nerve/audacity/cheek to say").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 tangential is an adjective (meaning only slightly relevant, going off at a tangent); a noun is required after "the", so it fails grammatically as well as in meaning.

• Option 2 brightness = the quality of giving out light or of being clever; it makes no sense in a sentence of reproach.

• Option 4 fitness = the state of being physically healthy or suitable for a purpose; irrelevant here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of arrogance: haughtiness, insolence, conceit, hubris, audacity, effrontery.

• Antonyms of arrogance: humility, modesty, meekness, diffidence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The show played to full houses for a five-night run and ended to ______ applause on Saturday night.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. tumultuous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tumultuous" means very loud, noisy and excited; uproarious. (शोरगुल भरा / जोरदार)

◦ Correct: The show played to full houses for a five-night run and ended to tumultuous applause on Saturday night.

• "Tumultuous applause" is a standard collocation for the thunderous clapping of a delighted audience — perfectly suited to a show that played to full houses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 semantic = relating to the meaning of words; "semantic applause" is meaningless.

• Option 2 redress = compensation or remedy for a wrong (noun/verb); it cannot describe applause.

• Option 4 barren = unable to produce crops or offspring; bleak and empty. It contradicts the positive context of full houses.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with applause: thunderous / rapturous / tumultuous / rousing / deafening / spontaneous applause.

• Synonyms of tumultuous: uproarious, boisterous, riotous, clamorous, turbulent. Antonyms: peaceful, quiet, orderly, subdued.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

He lights his pipe, (and on many an evenings he helps me with) dishes.
option_1: and on many evenings he helped me with the
option_2: and on many evenings he helps me with the
option_3: and many an evenings he helps me with the
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. and on many evenings he helps me with the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two errors have to be repaired in the bracketed part:

◦ "many an" must always be followed by a singular noun ("many an evening"), so "many an evenings" is wrong. The natural correction is the plural phrase "many evenings".

◦ The countable noun "dishes" needs the definite article: "helps me with the dishes" (the standard expression for washing up).

• The main clause "He lights his pipe" is in the simple present, so the coordinated verb must also stay in the simple present — "helps", not "helped".

◦ Correct: He lights his pipe, and on many evenings he helps me with the dishes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses "helped" (past), breaking the tense parallelism with "lights".

• Option 3 retains the faulty "many an evenings" (determiner-number clash).

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because the original contains both the "many an + plural" error and the missing article.

NOTE

• Rule: many a / many an + singular noun + singular verb — "Many a student has passed." Compare: many + plural noun + plural verb — "Many students have passed."

• "Do/wash the dishes" is a fixed expression and always takes "the".

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Nothing great in the world/ have been accomplished/ without passion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. have been accomplished.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "Nothing", an indefinite pronoun that is always singular. A singular subject requires the singular auxiliary "has".

◦ Correct: Nothing great in the world has been accomplished without passion.

• The words "in the world" form a prepositional phrase; the verb never agrees with the noun inside such a phrase — it agrees with the head subject "Nothing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment "Nothing great in the world" is correct — the adjective "great" rightly follows the indefinite pronoun (nothing great, something new, anybody else).

• Segment "without passion." is correct — "without" properly takes the uncountable noun "passion" with no article.

NOTE

• Indefinite pronouns that always take a singular verb: nothing, something, anything, everything, nobody, no one, somebody, someone, anybody, anyone, everybody, everyone, each, either, neither.

◦ Everyone has arrived. / Neither of the boys is guilty. / Nothing has changed.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

That is not a solution available (to most people for who email has become necessity.)
option_1: to most people for who email has become a necessity.
option_2: to most people for whom email has become a necessity.
option_3: for most people to whom email has became necessity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to most people for whom email has become a necessity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a preposition ("for"), the objective form of the relative pronoun is required — that is "whom", never "who".

◦ Correct: That is not a solution available to most people for whom email has become a necessity.

• The countable singular noun "necessity" also needs the indefinite article: "has become a necessity".

• Option 2 fixes both faults of the original: who → whom, and necessity → a necessity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong pronoun "for who".

• Option 3 has two problems: the preposition pair "for most people to whom" distorts the sense, and "has became" is wrong — after "has" the past participle "become" is needed (become – became – become).

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence as printed does contain errors.

NOTE

• Rule: use "who" as the subject (the man who called), and "whom" as the object or after a preposition (the man whom I called / the man to whom I spoke).

• Quick test: if you can replace it with "he/she", use who; if with "him/her", use whom.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Glorify
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Celebrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Glorify" means to praise highly, to honour, to exalt or extol somebody/something. (महिमामंडित करना / गुणगान करना)

• "Celebrate" also means to praise or honour publicly, to mark something with admiration. (प्रशंसा करना / उत्सव मनाना)

◦ Example: The poem glorifies (celebrates) the courage of the soldiers.

• Both verbs share the core idea of raising something in public esteem, so they are synonyms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Mock = to laugh at somebody in an unkind way; ridicule — an antonym of glorify.

• Option 2 Lower = to reduce in height, amount or status — again the opposite of exalting.

• Option 3 Wonder = to feel curiosity or amazement; it expresses surprise, not praise.

NOTE

• Synonyms of glorify: exalt, extol, laud, eulogise, venerate, celebrate, magnify.

• Antonyms of glorify: mock, ridicule, condemn, denigrate, disparage, belittle, vilify.

question: Four words are given, out of which three words are spelt correctly. Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ACQIUANT.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "ACQUAINT", not "ACQIUANT" — the letters U and I have been swapped in the printed option.

• "Acquaint" means to make somebody familiar with or aware of something. (परिचित कराना)

◦ Spelling key: A-C-Q-U-A-I-N-T. Remember that in English, Q is almost always followed by U, so "ACQIUANT" is impossible.

◦ Example: Please acquaint yourself with the rules before the exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 RESISTANCE is correctly spelt — the power to resist; note the ending -ance (not -ence).

• Option 3 PERSISTENT is correctly spelt — continuing firmly; note the ending -ent (not -ant).

• Option 4 PRIVILEGE is correctly spelt — a special right; note there is no "d" (never "priviledge").

NOTE

• Related forms: acquaint (verb) → acquaintance (noun: a person one knows slightly) → acquainted (adjective).

• Other "acqu-" words that follow the Q + U rule: acquire, acquisition, acquit, acquiesce.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

There are already many examples of great technology that had born in the United States.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of great technology that had.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "bear" in the sense of to be born / to come into existence is used in the passive voice: "was/were born" or "has/have/had been born". The active "had born" is wrong.

◦ Correct: There are already many examples of great technology that was born in the United States.

• Since the technology did not give birth to itself, the structure must be passive; the erroneous segment is therefore the one containing "that had".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "There are already many examples" is correct — the plural "examples" agrees with "There are", and "already" is properly placed.

• Segment "born in the United States." is correct in itself; the fault lies in the auxiliary that precedes it.

NOTE

• Forms of the verb: bear – bore – borne (to carry, to endure) and bear – bore – born (to give birth to, used passively).

◦ She has borne the pain bravely. (endured)

◦ He was born in Delhi. (birth — always passive)

• Never write "he had born" or "he has born" for birth; use "was born" / "had been born".

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: They were meant, she says, to be “a public display of your allegaince.”
option_2: They fly around like nobody 's buisness.
option_3: They also show problem behaviours, like physical aggression and cheating.
option_4: This guide offers sugestions of capital interest to travelers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. They also show problem behaviours, like physical aggression and cheating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 3 is spelt correctly — behaviours (British spelling of behaviors), physical, aggression (double g, double s) and cheating are all standard forms.

• Each of the other three sentences carries exactly one misspelt word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "allegaince" is wrong → the correct spelling is "allegiance" (loyalty to a person, country or cause). Remember the sequence -gia-, as in "alle-gia-nce".

• Option 2: "buisness" is wrong → the correct spelling is "business" (BUSI + NESS, from "busy").

• Option 4: "sugestions" is wrong → the correct spelling is "suggestions" (double g: SUG-G-ESTION).

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt words in SSC exams: allegiance, business, suggestion, occurrence, embarrassment, maintenance, questionnaire, privilege, accommodation, receive, separate, definitely.

• Note that "behaviour / behavior" and "traveller / traveler" are both acceptable (British vs American), so they are not treated as errors.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

A storm in a tea cup
option_1: Great outrage or excitement about a trivial matter
option_2: Constant source of annoyance to someone
option_3: To deal with a person who is more than one's match
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Great outrage or excitement about a trivial matter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a storm in a tea cup" means a great fuss, anger or excitement made over a very small or unimportant matter. (छोटी-सी बात पर बड़ा हंगामा)

◦ Example: The quarrel between the two neighbours over a parking space was just a storm in a tea cup.

• The image itself explains the sense — a mighty "storm" confined to something as tiny as a "tea cup", i.e. a disproportionate reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Constant source of annoyance to someone" is the meaning of "a thorn in one's flesh/side".

• Option 3 "To deal with a person who is more than one's match" corresponds to "to meet one's match".

• Option 4 "Back to original position" corresponds to "back to square one".

NOTE

• The American variant of this idiom is "a tempest in a teapot".

• Idioms of exaggeration: make a mountain out of a molehill (exaggerate a small problem), much ado about nothing, blow something out of proportion.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Most of the oil and gas that the UK ______ does not come from Russia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. imports.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states a general, present-day fact, so the simple present tense is required.

• The subject of the relative clause is "the UK", a singular noun (the name of one country), and a singular subject in the simple present takes the -s form of the verb: "the UK imports".

◦ Correct: Most of the oil and gas that the UK imports does not come from Russia.

• Notice the main verb "does not come" — it too is singular present, confirming that the whole sentence is in the present tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "import" is the plural/base form and would need a plural subject ("the countries import").

• Option 3 "importing" is a participle and cannot stand alone as the finite verb of the clause without an auxiliary ("is importing").

• Option 4 "imported" (past) clashes with the present-tense main verb "does not come".

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement rule: singular subject + verb + s/es in the simple present (He plays, The UK imports); plural subject + base verb (They play, The countries import).

• Names of countries, organisations and uncountable ideas are treated as singular in standard usage.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Opposing or taking arms against a government or ruler.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rebel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "rebel" is a person who rises in opposition or armed resistance against an established government or ruler. (विद्रोही / बागी)

◦ The verb "to rebel" means to fight against authority; the related noun is "rebellion" (विद्रोह).

◦ Example: The rebels captured the fort and refused to obey the king.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Volunteer = a person who offers to do something willingly and usually without pay. (स्वयंसेवक)

• Option 3 Rubel is not an English word in this sense; "rouble/ruble" is the currency of Russia — a distractor based on similar sound.

• Option 4 Participant = a person who takes part in an activity or event. (प्रतिभागी)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions:

◦ Rebel — one who takes up arms against the government

◦ Traitor — one who betrays his own country

◦ Mutiny — a revolt by soldiers or sailors against their officers

◦ Insurgent — a rebel taking part in an armed uprising

◦ Anarchist — one who wishes to abolish all government

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Equality and freedom have both been identified as important (1) ______ of democracy since ancient times. These principles are reflected in all citizens being (2) ______ before the law and having equal access to (3) ______ processes. For example, in a representative democracy, (4) ______ vote has equal weight, no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a (5) ______, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties which are generally protected by a constitution.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. characteristics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Characteristics" means typical or distinguishing features or qualities of something. (विशेषताएँ / लक्षण)

◦ Correct: Equality and freedom have both been identified as important characteristics of democracy since ancient times.

• Equality and freedom are the defining qualities of a democracy, and the very next sentence explains how these "principles are reflected" in citizens' lives — confirming that the blank needs a word for defining features.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 statistics = numerical data collected and analysed; equality and freedom are values, not figures.

• Option 3 analytics = the systematic computational analysis of data; irrelevant to political values.

• Option 4 linguistics = the scientific study of language; unrelated to the passage.

NOTE

• Word family: character → characteristic (adjective/noun) → characterise (verb, to describe the qualities of).

• Similar words for defining qualities: attributes, traits, features, hallmarks, properties.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Equality and freedom have both been identified as important (1) ______ of democracy since ancient times. These principles are reflected in all citizens being (2) ______ before the law and having equal access to (3) ______ processes. For example, in a representative democracy, (4) ______ vote has equal weight, no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a (5) ______, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties which are generally protected by a constitution.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. equal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase required is "equal before the law" — the well-known principle that all citizens are treated alike by the legal system, with no special favour or discrimination. (कानून के समक्ष समानता)

◦ Correct: These principles are reflected in all citizens being equal before the law and having equal access to legislative processes.

• The sentence begins "These principles", referring back to equality and freedom; so the blank must express equality, not its opposite.

• The parallel phrase later in the same sentence — "having equal access" — is a further clue that the writer is describing sameness of treatment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 irregular, 3 unfair and 4 unequal are all negative words. Inserting any of them would contradict the passage, which is praising democracy for guaranteeing equality.

• "Unequal before the law" would in fact describe an undemocratic system.

NOTE

• The idea in the blank corresponds to Article 14 of the Indian Constitution: "equality before the law and equal protection of the laws" — a favourite SSC cross-link between English comprehension and Polity.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Equality and freedom have both been identified as important (1) ______ of democracy since ancient times. These principles are reflected in all citizens being (2) ______ before the law and having equal access to (3) ______ processes. For example, in a representative democracy, (4) ______ vote has equal weight, no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a (5) ______, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties which are generally protected by a constitution.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. legislative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Legislative" means relating to the making of laws or to the body that makes them (the legislature). (विधायी)

◦ Correct: ... all citizens being equal before the law and having equal access to legislative processes.

• Democracy guarantees every citizen a share in law-making — the right to vote, to contest elections and to petition the legislature. The passage's own next sentence ("in a representative democracy, every vote has equal weight ... anyone seeking to become a representative") is precisely about legislative participation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 copulative = (in grammar) joining or linking, as with a linking verb; technical and irrelevant here.

• Option 2 relative = considered in relation to something else; "relative processes" carries no clear political meaning.

• Option 4 perennial = lasting for a very long time or recurring every year; it describes duration, not a democratic process.

NOTE

• The three organs of government, often tested in SSC: Legislature (makes laws), Executive (implements laws) and Judiciary (interprets laws). Their adjectives are legislative, executive and judicial.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Equality and freedom have both been identified as important (1) ______ of democracy since ancient times. These principles are reflected in all citizens being (2) ______ before the law and having equal access to (3) ______ processes. For example, in a representative democracy, (4) ______ vote has equal weight, no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a (5) ______, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties which are generally protected by a constitution.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. every.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun after the blank is the singular countable noun "vote", followed by the singular verb "has". Only a determiner that takes a singular countable noun can fit — and that is "every".

◦ Correct: For example, in a representative democracy, every vote has equal weight ...

• The sense is also exactly right: in a democracy each and every single vote counts the same, which is the principle of "one person, one vote, one value".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 few takes a plural noun and plural verb ("few votes have"), and it also wrongly suggests a small number.

• Option 3 much is used with uncountable nouns ("much water"), never with "vote".

• Option 4 all likewise requires the plural ("all votes have"), so it clashes with the singular "vote has".

NOTE

• Determiner rules for SSC:

◦ every / each / either / neither / one + singular countable noun + singular verb

◦ many / few / several / all / both + plural countable noun + plural verb

◦ much / little / a great deal of + uncountable noun + singular verb

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Equality and freedom have both been identified as important (1) ______ of democracy since ancient times. These principles are reflected in all citizens being (2) ______ before the law and having equal access to (3) ______ processes. For example, in a representative democracy, (4) ______ vote has equal weight, no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a (5) ______, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties which are generally protected by a constitution.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. representative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the singular article "a", so only a singular noun can be used — which at once rules out the plural options.

◦ Correct: ... no unreasonable restrictions can apply to anyone seeking to become a representative, and the freedom of its citizens is secured by legitimized rights and liberties ...

• The context is a "representative democracy" (mentioned in the very same sentence), in which citizens elect representatives to make laws for them. Saying that anyone may seek to become a representative is the natural completion of the idea of equal access to legislative processes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 peasants and Option 3 rulers are plural and cannot follow "a"; besides, becoming a peasant is not a democratic office.

• Option 4 dictators is plural as well, and a dictator is the very antithesis of democracy — a ruler with absolute, unelected power.

NOTE

• Grammar point: the indefinite article a/an is used only with singular countable nouns. Use a before a consonant sound (a representative) and an before a vowel sound (an elector).

• Static link: India follows a representative parliamentary democracy, in which citizens elect members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution provides freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 26.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 26 of the Indian Constitution grants every religious denomination (or any section of it) the freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion. (धार्मिक मामलों के प्रबंधन की स्वतंत्रता)

• Subject to public order, morality and health, Article 26 gives every religious denomination the right:

◦ (a) to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes;

◦ (b) to manage its own affairs in matters of religion;

◦ (c) to own and acquire movable and immovable property;

◦ (d) to administer such property in accordance with law.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty — no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

• Article 37 falls under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) and declares that the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

NOTE

• The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered by Articles 25 to 28:

◦ Article 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion

◦ Article 26 — freedom to manage religious affairs

◦ Article 27 — freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion

◦ Article 28 — freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions

question: If Birth rate of a country is more than death rate then the population will ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is increase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Natural growth of population = Birth rate − Death rate. When the birth rate exceeds the death rate, the natural growth rate is positive, so the population increases. (जनसंख्या में वृद्धि होगी)

• Birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 people in a year; death rate (mortality rate) is the number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.

◦ Example: If the birth rate is 20 per 1,000 and the death rate is 7 per 1,000, the natural growth rate is 13 per 1,000, i.e. 1.3 per cent annual growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• If the death rate is higher than the birth rate, the population declines (as in Japan and several European countries today).

• If the two rates are equal, the population remains stationary in natural terms.

• Actual population change also depends on migration: Population change = (Births − Deaths) + (Immigration − Emigration).

NOTE

• India's population growth is studied through the Census (held every 10 years; the last completed census was in 2011) and the Sample Registration System (SRS) of the Registrar General of India.

• The demographic transition theory explains how societies move from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as they develop.

question: Tribal leader Birsa was associated with which tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Munda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Birsa Munda (1875–1900) was a tribal freedom fighter and religious leader belonging to the Munda tribe of the Chhotanagpur plateau (present-day Jharkhand). (बिरसा मुंडा — मुंडा जनजाति)

• He led the Ulgulan ("The Great Tumult") movement, 1899–1900, against British land policies, forced labour (begari) and the exploitation of tribals by dikus (outsiders) and moneylenders.

• His followers revered him as "Dharti Aaba" (Father of the Earth) and as Bhagwan Birsa.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900. His struggle contributed to the passing of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, which restricted the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals.

• 15 November, his birth anniversary, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (Tribal Pride Day); it is also the foundation day of Jharkhand (created in 2000).

• The Bhils are concentrated in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat; the Gonds mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra; the Bhutias in Sikkim and northern West Bengal.

NOTE

• Other major tribal uprisings: Santhal Rebellion (1855–56) led by Sidhu and Kanhu; Kol Uprising (1831–32); Rampa Rebellion (1922–24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju; Tana Bhagat movement (1914) led by Jatra Bhagat.

question: Which among the following novels was written by famous Indian author Mulk Raj Anand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Untouchable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Untouchable" (1935) is the celebrated first novel of Mulk Raj Anand. It portrays a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper, and exposes the cruelty of untouchability and the caste system. (अछूत — मुल्क राज आनंद)

• The novel carried a preface by the English poet E. M. Forster and made Anand one of the pioneers of Indian writing in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "The Room on the Roof" was written by Ruskin Bond; it won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957 when Bond was only 21.

• Option 3 "Train to Pakistan" (1956) was written by Khushwant Singh and depicts the horrors of the Partition of 1947 in the fictional village of Mano Majra.

• Option 4 "Godan" (1936) is the masterpiece of Munshi Premchand, written in Hindi, about the peasant Hori and rural indebtedness.

NOTE

• Other works of Mulk Raj Anand: Coolie (1936), Two Leaves and a Bud (1937), The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle, The Private Life of an Indian Prince.

• Anand, R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao are together called the "trinity" of early Indian English fiction. Anand received the Padma Bhushan in 1968.

question: Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by the Government of Meghalaya to support landless and marginal families by providing them with piglets and inputs for rearing pigs in their backyards. (मेघालय — ग्रामीण बैकयार्ड सूकर पालन योजना)

• The aim is to raise household income, nutrition and self-employment in rural areas, since pork is a staple food and pig rearing is a traditional livelihood in Meghalaya and the North-East.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya ("the abode of clouds") was carved out of Assam and became a full state on 21 January 1972. Its capital is Shillong.

• Meghalaya is famous for Cherrapunji (Sohra) and Mawsynram, among the wettest places on Earth, and for its living root bridges.

• The state's main tribes are the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo, all of which follow a matrilineal system of inheritance.

NOTE

• Related national livestock schemes: National Livestock Mission, Rashtriya Gokul Mission (indigenous cattle), Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) and the National Animal Disease Control Programme.

question: Which sea separates Africa from the Arabian peninsula?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red Sea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Red Sea is a narrow inlet of the Indian Ocean lying between north-eastern Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). (लाल सागर)

• It is connected to the Mediterranean Sea in the north through the Suez Canal and to the Arabian Sea / Gulf of Aden in the south through the strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

• The Red Sea occupies part of the Great Rift Valley system and is one of the saltiest and warmest seas in the world, because it receives almost no river water and suffers high evaporation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Black Sea lies between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, connected to the Mediterranean by the Bosphorus Strait, Sea of Marmara and Dardanelles.

• The White Sea is an inlet of the Arctic Ocean on the north-western coast of Russia (port of Arkhangelsk).

• The Caspian Sea, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan, is the largest inland water body (lake) in the world.

NOTE

• The Suez Canal (opened 1869, in Egypt) links the Red Sea with the Mediterranean and is one of the world's busiest shipping routes.

• The Red Sea gets its name from seasonal blooms of the reddish alga Trichodesmium erythraeum.

question: Which among the following terms means growing of fruits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pomiculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pomiculture" is the cultivation of fruits — the science and practice of growing fruit crops. (फल उत्पादन)

◦ It comes from the Latin pomum meaning "fruit". It is also called fruit culture and is a branch of horticulture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Apiculture = the rearing of honey bees for honey and wax. (मधुमक्खी पालन)

• Option 2 Arboriculture = the cultivation and care of trees and shrubs, especially for ornamental purposes. (वृक्ष संवर्धन)

• Option 4 Sericulture = the rearing of silkworms for the production of raw silk. (रेशम कीट पालन)

NOTE

• Other "-culture" terms frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Horticulture — growing of garden crops (fruits, vegetables, flowers)

◦ Floriculture — growing of flowers

◦ Olericulture — growing of vegetables

◦ Viticulture — growing of grapes

◦ Pisciculture — rearing of fish

◦ Aquaculture — farming of aquatic organisms

◦ Vermiculture — rearing of earthworms for compost

question: “Chhath Puja” is celebrated with great grandeur all over the world mainly by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihari community.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is a four-day festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his sister Chhathi Maiya (Usha), celebrated chiefly by the Bihari community and by people of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and the Nepal Terai. (छठ पूजा — बिहार)

• It is observed on the Shashthi (sixth day) of the Hindu month of Kartika (October–November); a smaller Chaiti Chhath falls in the month of Chaitra.

• The four days are Nahay-Khay, Kharna (Lohanda), Sandhya Arghya (offering to the setting sun) and Usha Arghya (offering to the rising sun) — Chhath is the only festival in which the setting sun is also worshipped.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Devotees observe a rigorous fast, often without even water (nirjala), and stand in rivers or ponds to offer arghya.

• With the migration of Bihari families, Chhath is now celebrated in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Mauritius, Fiji, Trinidad, Guyana, Suriname and the USA.

NOTE

• Other major regional festivals for SSC: Bihu (Assam), Onam (Kerala), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Baisakhi (Punjab), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Bihula and Sama-Chakeva (Bihar), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland).

question: Shri Bhagwant Mann became the Chief Minister of which state in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Punjab on 16 March 2022. (भगवंत मान — पंजाब के मुख्यमंत्री)

• He took the oath at Khatkar Kalan, the ancestral village of Shaheed Bhagat Singh, in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar district.

• In the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, AAP won 92 of the 117 seats, a landslide that ended the Congress government led by Charanjit Singh Channi. Mann himself won from the Dhuri constituency.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Before entering politics as a leader, Bhagwant Mann was a well-known comedian; he had earlier been a Member of Parliament from Sangrur (2014 and 2019).

• Punjab: capital Chandigarh (shared with Haryana), 117 Assembly seats, 13 Lok Sabha seats, 7 Rajya Sabha seats.

• Governor of Punjab at the time of the swearing-in: Banwarilal Purohit.

NOTE

• Other results of the 2022 Assembly elections: Yogi Adityanath returned as CM of Uttar Pradesh, Pushkar Singh Dhami in Uttarakhand, Pramod Sawant in Goa and N. Biren Singh in Manipur.

question: England lift the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 trophy after beating ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• England won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 by defeating Pakistan by 5 wickets in the final played at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), Australia, on 13 November 2022. (इंग्लैंड ने पाकिस्तान को हराया)

• Pakistan scored 137/8; England chased it down in 19 overs. Ben Stokes made an unbeaten 52 and Sam Curran took 3/12, winning both the Player of the Match and Player of the Tournament awards.

• England were captained by Jos Buttler; Pakistan by Babar Azam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• With this win, England became the first team to hold the ODI World Cup (2019) and the T20 World Cup (2022) at the same time. It was England's second T20 World Cup title (the first was in 2010).

• India lost to England by 10 wickets in the semi-final; New Zealand lost to Pakistan in the other semi-final.

• The 2021 T20 World Cup was won by Australia (beating New Zealand); the 2024 edition was won by India (beating South Africa).

NOTE

• T20 World Cup winners: 2007 India, 2009 Pakistan, 2010 England, 2012 West Indies, 2014 Sri Lanka, 2016 West Indies, 2021 Australia, 2022 England, 2024 India.

question: Which two head rivers merge to form the river Ganga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alaknanda and Bhagirathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ganga is formed by the confluence of the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda at Devprayag in Uttarakhand; downstream of Devprayag the river is called the Ganga. (देवप्रयाग — भागीरथी + अलकनंदा = गंगा)

• The Bhagirathi rises from the Gaumukh snout of the Gangotri glacier; the Alaknanda rises near the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers above Badrinath.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Panch Prayag (five confluences) of the Alaknanda in Uttarakhand:

◦ Vishnuprayag — Alaknanda + Dhauliganga

◦ Nandprayag — Alaknanda + Nandakini

◦ Karnaprayag — Alaknanda + Pindar

◦ Rudraprayag — Alaknanda + Mandakini

◦ Devprayag — Alaknanda + Bhagirathi (the Ganga is born here)

• The Ganga is about 2,525 km long; it enters the plains at Haridwar and forms, with the Brahmaputra and Meghna, the world's largest delta, the Sundarbans.

NOTE

• Major left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda. Major right-bank tributaries: Yamuna, Son, Punpun.

• The Ganga was declared India's National River in 2008; the Namami Gange programme was launched in 2014.

question: Which among the following acids is found in Mustard oil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Erucic Acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Erucic acid is a long-chain monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid that occurs naturally in mustard oil and rapeseed oil, where it may form 40–50 per cent of the total fatty acids. (सरसों के तेल में इरूसिक अम्ल)

• In large amounts erucic acid is considered harmful to the heart, which is why low-erucic-acid rapeseed (canola) varieties were developed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Malic acid is found in apples and other fruits (Latin malum = apple).

• Option 2 Tartaric acid is found in tamarind and grapes; it is a component of baking powder.

• Option 3 Lauric acid is found chiefly in coconut oil and palm kernel oil.

NOTE

• Common natural acids asked in SSC:

◦ Citric acid — lemon, orange

◦ Acetic acid — vinegar

◦ Lactic acid — curd/milk, and in muscles during fatigue

◦ Oxalic acid — tomato, spinach

◦ Formic acid — ant sting and nettle

◦ Butyric acid — rancid butter

◦ Uric acid — urine (excess causes gout)

question: What is the atomic number of Nitrogen in the science periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nitrogen (N) has the atomic number 7, meaning each nitrogen atom contains 7 protons in its nucleus. Its atomic mass is about 14 u, so it also has 7 neutrons in its commonest isotope. (नाइट्रोजन — परमाणु क्रमांक 7)

• Electronic configuration: 2, 5 — it therefore lies in Group 15 (VA) and Period 2 of the modern periodic table.

• Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of the Earth's atmosphere by volume and exists as the very stable diatomic molecule N₂ with a triple bond.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 21 is the atomic number of Scandium (Sc).

• Option 3 18 is the atomic number of Argon (Ar), a noble gas.

• Option 4 11 is the atomic number of Sodium (Na).

NOTE

• Atomic numbers worth memorising: H = 1, He = 2, C = 6, N = 7, O = 8, F = 9, Ne = 10, Na = 11, Mg = 12, Al = 13, Si = 14, P = 15, S = 16, Cl = 17, Ar = 18, K = 19, Ca = 20.

• Nitrogen was discovered by Daniel Rutherford (1772). Liquid nitrogen (boiling point −196 °C) is used as a cryogenic coolant, and nitrogen is essential for making ammonia (Haber process) and fertilisers such as urea.

question: Kuchipudi dance is accompanied by which type of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, is performed to Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India. (कुचिपुड़ी — कर्नाटक संगीत)

• The accompanying instruments typically include the mridangam, violin, veena, flute and cymbals (talam), with a vocalist singing in Telugu or Sanskrit.

• Kuchipudi takes its name from the village of Kuchelapuram in Krishna district; it was systematised in the 17th century by Siddhendra Yogi, whose famous dance-drama is Bhama Kalapam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A signature item of Kuchipudi is the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs while balancing a pot of water on the head and dancing on the rim of a brass plate.

• Famous exponents: Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu, Swapnasundari.

NOTE

• Classical dances and their music:

◦ Carnatic music — Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kathakali (Kerala)

◦ Hindustani music — Kathak (North India), Odissi is accompanied by Odissi music, Manipuri by Manipuri traditions, and Sattriya by Assamese Borgeet.

question: In which country was the first Olympic Games held in the year 1896?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greece.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, from 6 to 15 April 1896. (यूनान — प्रथम आधुनिक ओलंपिक)

• They were organised at the initiative of the French educationist Baron Pierre de Coubertin, who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894 at the Sorbonne, Paris.

• About 241 athletes from 14 nations took part in 43 events across 9 sports. The main venue was the restored Panathenaic Stadium.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ancient Olympic Games began in 776 BCE at Olympia in Greece in honour of Zeus and were abolished in 393 CE by Emperor Theodosius I.

• The first Olympic champion of the modern era was James Connolly (USA, triple jump). Greece's Spyridon Louis won the first marathon.

• The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius — Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together); the five interlocking rings represent the five inhabited continents.

NOTE

• The IOC headquarters is at Lausanne, Switzerland. Recent Summer Olympics: 2016 Rio de Janeiro, 2020 Tokyo (held in 2021), 2024 Paris; the 2028 Games go to Los Angeles.

question: Who is the playback singer and composer of the famous song “Qismat Ki Hawa” which featured in the movie Ludo in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C. Ramchandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The song "Qismat Ki Hawa Kabhi Naram Kabhi Garam" was composed and sung by C. Ramchandra for the film Albela (1951), and it was reused in Anurag Basu's 2020 film Ludo. (सी. रामचंद्र)

• C. Ramchandra (Ramchandra Narhar Chitalkar, 1918–1982) was a leading music director of the 1940s–50s who also sang under the name Chitalkar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• His most famous composition is the patriotic song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" (lyrics by Kavi Pradeep), sung by Lata Mangeshkar before Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963.

• Other well-known songs from Albela (1951): "Bholi Surat Dil Ke Khote", "Sham Dhale Khidki Tale", "Dheere Se Aaja Ri Akhiyan Mein".

• Ludo (2020) was directed by Anurag Basu and starred Abhishek Bachchan, Rajkummar Rao, Pankaj Tripathi, Aditya Roy Kapur and Fatima Sana Shaikh; it was released on Netflix.

NOTE

• Distractors: Arijit Singh is a contemporary playback singer ("Tum Hi Ho"); A. R. Rahman is an Oscar-winning composer ("Jai Ho"); R. D. Burman (Pancham) was the celebrated composer of the 1970s–80s ("Dum Maro Dum", "Piya Tu Ab To Aaja").

question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012) was the most celebrated guru of Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (1963) and took Kuchipudi from village dance-drama to the international solo concert stage, choreographing more than 180 solo items and 15 dance-dramas.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1998) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1967).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous exponents of other forms:

◦ Kathak — Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj

◦ Bharatanatyam — Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam

◦ Manipuri — Guru Bipin Singh, Nirmala Mehta, Jhaveri Sisters

• Kuchipudi originated in the village of Kuchelapuram (Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh) and was revived by Siddhendra Yogi.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in 1995 and was implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). (ग्रामीण रोजगार सृजन कार्यक्रम — 1995)

• Its objective was to create self-employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns by helping entrepreneurs set up village industries, with margin-money subsidy and bank credit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In 2008, REGP was merged with the Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) to form the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), a credit-linked subsidy scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME through KVIC as the nodal agency.

• KVIC was established in 1956 under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, with headquarters in Mumbai.

NOTE

• Other landmark employment/rural schemes and their years: IRDP (1978–79), JRY (1989), EAS (1993), SGSY (1999), SGRY (2001), NREGA/MGNREGA (2005, renamed 2009), NRLM–Aajeevika (2011), DDU-GKY (2014), PMEGP (2008).

question: Jyotiba Phule founded which of the following organizations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyashodhak Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Govindrao Phule (1827–1890) founded the Satyashodhak Samaj ("Society of Truth Seekers") at Pune on 24 September 1873. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिबा फुले)

• Its aims were to liberate the Shudras and Ati-Shudras from caste oppression and Brahminical domination, to promote education among the lower castes and women, and to make rituals simple and priest-free.

• Along with his wife Savitribai Phule — regarded as India's first woman teacher — he opened the first school for girls in Pune in 1848 and a home for widows and their children.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Phule's famous works: Gulamgiri (1873), Shetkaryacha Asud (Cultivator's Whipcord), Tritiya Ratna and Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak. He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888 by Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar.

• Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, with the slogan "Back to the Vedas".

• Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 at Calcutta.

• The Satnami movement was led by Ghasidas in Chhattisgarh (an earlier Satnami sect was founded by Birbhan in the 17th century).

NOTE

• Other social-reform bodies for SSC: Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867), Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897), Servants of India Society (Gopal Krishna Gokhale, 1905), Self-Respect Movement (E. V. Ramasamy 'Periyar', 1925).

question: Jeev Milkha Singh is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jeev Milkha Singh (born 15 December 1971) is a leading Indian professional golfer. (जीव मिल्खा सिंह — गोल्फ)

• He was the first Indian golfer to join the European Tour and the first Indian to play in all four major championships. He has won four European Tour titles and topped the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2006 and 2008.

• He received the Arjuna Award (1999) and the Padma Shri (2007).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He is the son of the legendary sprinter Milkha Singh, the "Flying Sikh", who won gold at the 1958 Commonwealth Games and 1958 & 1962 Asian Games and finished fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

• Other well-known Indian golfers: Anirban Lahiri, Shubhankar Sharma, Gaganjeet Bhullar, Arjun Atwal, Aditi Ashok (who finished fourth at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics).

NOTE

• Golf terms often asked: birdie (one under par), eagle (two under par), albatross (three under par), bogey (one over par), par, caddie, tee, putt, fairway, green.

• The four golf majors: The Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open and The Open Championship (British Open).

question: Cotton was probably grown at Mehrgarh from about ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7000 years ago.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mehrgarh, a Neolithic site on the Kacchi plain of Balochistan (present-day Pakistan), near the Bolan Pass, is the place where cotton was probably grown about 7,000 years ago. (मेहरगढ़ — लगभग 7000 वर्ष पूर्व कपास)

• NCERT history textbooks describe Mehrgarh as one of the earliest villages in the subcontinent, where people first began to grow wheat and barley and to rear sheep, goats and cattle.

• Mehrgarh was excavated by the French archaeologist Jean-François Jarrige from 1974 onwards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Burials at Mehrgarh show the dead placed with goats and beads, indicating belief in an afterlife; the site also yielded evidence of the world's earliest known dentistry (drilled teeth).

• Cotton later became a hallmark of the Harappan civilisation; actual cotton cloth fragments have been found at Mohenjo-daro, and cotton seeds at Mehrgarh. The Greeks called Indian cotton "sindon".

NOTE

• Key Harappan sites: Harappa (Ravi, Pakistan), Mohenjo-daro (Indus, Pakistan), Lothal (Gujarat — dockyard), Dholavira (Gujarat — water management, UNESCO site), Kalibangan (Rajasthan — ploughed field), Rakhigarhi (Haryana — largest Indian site), Banawali and Surkotada (horse bones).

question: Which among the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bryophyte.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bryophytes — the mosses, liverworts and hornworts — are called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" because although they live on land, they require water for sexual reproduction, since their motile male gametes (antherozoids) must swim to the egg. (ब्रायोफाइटा — पादप जगत के उभयचर)

• They lack true roots, stems and leaves and have no vascular tissue (no xylem or phloem); they are anchored by rhizoids.

• Examples: Funaria (moss), Marchantia and Riccia (liverworts), Sphagnum (bog moss, used as packing material and a source of peat).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Thallophyta (Option 3) are the simplest plants — algae and, in older classifications, fungi — with an undifferentiated thallus body.

• Gymnosperms (Option 1) are naked-seeded vascular plants such as Pinus, Cycas and Cedrus.

• Angiosperms (Option 4) are flowering plants whose seeds are enclosed in fruits; they are divided into monocots and dicots.

NOTE

• Whittaker's classification of the plant kingdom: Thallophyta → Bryophyta → Pteridophyta → Gymnosperms → Angiosperms.

• Pteridophytes (ferns) are called the "first true land plants" because they are the first group to possess vascular tissue.

question: The term “Vetti” in Chola empire is related to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is forced labour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Cholas, "Vetti" was a tax collected not in cash but in the form of forced/unpaid labour demanded from the villagers. (वेट्टि — बेगार / अवैतनिक श्रम)

• Another important Chola levy was "Kadamai", the land revenue paid by cultivators.

• These terms come from Chola inscriptions, especially those of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, and are part of the NCERT chapter on new kings and kingdoms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Cholas ruled from Thanjavur (Tanjore) in the Kaveri delta; the dynasty was founded in the 9th century by Vijayalaya Chola (c. 850 CE).

• Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE) built the Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site among the "Great Living Chola Temples".

• Rajendra I conquered up to the Ganga, took the title Gangaikonda Chola and built the new capital Gangaikonda Cholapuram; he also sent naval expeditions to Srivijaya (South-East Asia).

NOTE

• Chola local self-government was famous: the Ur (assembly of ordinary villagers), the Sabha (assembly of Brahmin villages, brahmadeya) and the Nagaram (assembly of merchants). The Uttaramerur inscriptions describe the elaborate election procedure (kudavolai system) of the Sabha's committees.

question: Who chairs the Monetary Policy Committee in India?
option_2: Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India
option_3: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor, Reserve Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of India is chaired by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक के गवर्नर)

• The MPC was constituted in 2016 under the RBI Act, 1934 (as amended by the Finance Act, 2016) and is responsible for fixing the policy repo rate to achieve the inflation target.

• It has six members: three from the RBI — the Governor (Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and an officer nominated by the Central Board — and three external members appointed by the Central Government for four years.

• Decisions are by majority vote; in case of a tie the Governor has a casting vote. The MPC must meet at least four times a year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's inflation target is 4 per cent CPI inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 per cent (i.e. 2–6 per cent), notified by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI every five years.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised on 1 January 1949. Its first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith and the first Indian Governor was C. D. Deshmukh.

NOTE

• Key monetary policy tools: Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), Bank rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Open Market Operations (OMO).

question: The Lok Sabha (House of the People) was duly constituted for the first time on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17 April 1952.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Lok Sabha was duly constituted on 17 April 1952, after the country's first general elections, which were held from October 1951 to February 1952. (प्रथम लोकसभा — 17 अप्रैल 1952)

• The first sitting of the House was held on 13 May 1952. Its first Speaker was G. V. Mavalankar, and the first Prime Minister of the elected House was Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The first Lok Sabha had 489 seats, of which the Indian National Congress won 364. India's first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Before 1952, the Constituent Assembly (which had adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949) served as the provisional Parliament of India.

• The Lok Sabha's maximum strength as per the Constitution is 552 (530 from States + 20 from Union Territories + 2 Anglo-Indians, the last category discontinued by the 104th Amendment, 2019). Present strength: 543.

• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, extendable by one year at a time during a National Emergency.

NOTE

• Related dates: the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day). The Rajya Sabha was first constituted on 3 April 1952.
